teaser: The meter now charges for what is read; the reader can pause, reset or mark it, and what was read folds away six ways, with a line and a paragraph per section.
core_idea: Once Dinis decided that a reader pays for what they read and not for what they scroll, the numbers had to be the reader's to correct: pause, reset and marks by hand; and once the newsroom knows what was read, it can step aside on a return visit or a scroll back up, in six views from a margin line to hidden, never while the reader reads forward, using a line and a paragraph written for every one of 1,897 sections.

nodes.label: Charge for what is read
nodes.summary: Dinis's decision: the meter charges for the share read, not the share scrolled; reading done on an earlier visit is not charged again.

nodes.label: The meter, v1.5.0
nodes.summary: A new versioned meter whose page view settles the charge to the share read beyond what was read before, up or down.

nodes.label: The reader in control
nodes.summary: The measure can be wrong both ways, so the reader can correct it.

nodes.label: Pause, kept
nodes.summary: Stops all measuring on every page until resumed, across reloads.

nodes.label: Reset and marks
nodes.summary: A page back to unread with a refund to the minimum; any section marked read or unread by hand.

nodes.label: Six views of what was read
nodes.summary: Full, Margin, Faded, Paragraph, Line and Hidden, chosen by the reader and kept in the browser.

nodes.label: Never while reading forward
nodes.summary: The views switch on only on a return visit or a scroll back up, and a section on screen is never folded by the clock.

nodes.label: The words in view stay
nodes.summary: Before a fold the first visible element is noted, and the scroll is corrected after it.

nodes.label: A line and a paragraph per section
nodes.summary: 1,897 sections in 174 articles, each with about eight words and two or three sentences that say what it says.

nodes.label: Fourteen agents
nodes.summary: Each read a batch of articles and wrote their summaries; a script checked length, wording and coverage.

nodes.label: A summary knows it is stale
nodes.summary: Each carries a hash of its section; a corrected section marks its summary stale.

nodes.label: Summaries with every article
nodes.summary: The authoring guide asks for summaries beside the graph, and the build counts extracts.

quotes.text: Nothing on the page changes while you go down it.
quotes.why: The rule that makes the views safe to switch on.

quotes.text: A summary knows when it is out of date.
quotes.why: Why a correction to an article cannot leave its summary lying.
